statement: The Kingdom of Sicily passed from the Norman Hauteville dynasty to the Hohenstaufen (Staufen) when Constance — the posthumous daughter of Roger II of Sicily and heiress of the Norman kingdom — married Henry VI of Germany (1186). Henry VI conquered Sicily (1194) despite resistance; their son Frederick II was raised in Sicily and became Emperor Frederick II — simultaneously Holy Roman Emperor and King of Sicily/Naples. The union of imperial and Sicilian power was the papacy's greatest nightmare: encirclement of the Papal States. It drove the catastrophic pope-emperor conflict (1239–1250).
